proposed.explanation: REQ-4-4 requires a new file path to be rejected when it 'must not conflict with an existing file or directory on the current branch', and a rejected submission must not change files, branch head or commit history. On the seeded repository alice-dev/acme-docs the branch main already contains 'src/search.ts', so 'src' is an existing directory on that branch. The editor's validation only compares against exact file paths, so submitting File name 'src' creates a file plus a commit at a path that collides with the existing directory, instead of reporting the invalid path. The fixture is valid: the repository is public, alice-dev owns it (repository Admin), branch main exists with the seeded files, no file named 'src' exists, and the control submission with a unique path through the same action succeeds.
proposed.subject: saveFile
proposed.requirement_text:
This feature builds on the persisted objects, opened pages, or authenticated-session context provided by REQ-4-1 (Browse Repository Files and Directories) and REQ-1-1-2 (Sign In with an Existing Account); it must reuse that context and keep pages and data consistent after the context changes. The file editor is the form opened from Edit or Add file on the Code page; the user edits file content at a path on the current branch and submits it. Only Write, Maintain, Admin, or organization Owner may submit; Read and Triage may only view. A single submission stores the file-path and content change, commit message, author, parent commit, and target branch as one indivisible record and moves the target branch to point to that new commit. A new or renamed file path must not be empty, must not begin with `/`, must not contain a `..` path segment, and must not conflict with an existing file or directory on the current branch; the commit message must contain 1–72 non-empty characters after trimming leading and trailing whitespace. If the path conflicts, content validation fails, the commit message is noncompliant, the branch is protected, or persistence fails, the page displays the reason and does not change the file, branch head, or commit history. An invalid path displays “Invalid file path”, and an empty commit message displays “Commit message is required”. From the writable Code page, the unique “Add file” button opens the “Create new file” menuitem. The editor has a field labeled “File name”, a textbox named “File contents”, an initially empty field labeled “Commit message”, and a “Commit changes” button. Creating a unique file such as `pw-file-<unique suffix>.md` with nonempty text and a message such as `Add <file name>` immediately opens a view displaying the exact saved content. Its “Commits” link opens history displaying the exact submitted message. Submitting `../invalid.md` with content `must not be saved` and no commit message reports the invalid path and/or required message and changes neither files nor history. The example content is ordinary text, not a forbidden content value by itself; rejection follows from the invalid path or missing message.

Screenshot reference:
![image](reference/github-web-file-editor.png)

proposed.explanation: REQ-6-6 states that a merged pull request is terminal: 'Merged is terminal, the page does not display close or reopen operations, and the server rejects status changes.' The reopen-pr handler performs no terminal-state check, so invoking it for a Merged pull request rewrites the persisted status to Open, which also makes the PR mergeable/closeable again. The fixture is valid: rd-p1 (seed title 'Improve onboarding', authored by the signed-in account alice-dev, repository acme-docs which is public and readable) is already in the legitimately persisted Merged state, no branch or commit has been changed for it, and the control shows the same handler correctly reopens an ordinary Closed pull request authored by the same user, so the arguments and actor satisfy every prerequisite.
proposed.subject: reopenPR
proposed.requirement_text: The PR page provides Close pull request and Reopen pull request as buttons for authorized users. Close pull request immediately sets Closed without an extra confirmation dialog, then Reopen pull request immediately restores Open. After reload, Close pull request is available again. For a viewer who is neither author nor Maintain/Admin/Owner, both controls are absent, rather than merely disabled or rejected after activation. Seed data supplies the author and a separate Read viewer, an authored Open PR for the close/reopen cycle, and a separate Open PR readable by that viewer for permission validation. When the proposed change should not proceed, the PR author, Maintain, Admin, or organization Owner may close an unmerged Open or Draft PR without merging; the same roles may reopen a Closed PR as Open. The system stores the status, operator, and time and records the transition, while keeping the PR discussion, reviews, diff, and branch references viewable; closing or reopening must not update any branch. Merged is terminal, the page does not display close or reopen operations, and the server rejects status changes. This feature builds on the persisted objects, opened pages, or authenticated-session context provided by REQ-6-2-3 (Create a Pull Request from Comparison Results) and REQ-1-1-2 (Sign In with an Existing Account); it must reuse that context and keep pages and data consistent after the context changes.

proposed.explanation: REQ-5-4 and the REQ-5 role lists are explicit that status changes are restricted to Triage, Maintain, Admin (or organization Owner): 'Write and Read users may only view the status' and 'the server rejects their submissions'. The issue status handler applies no role check at all, and the surrounding permission helper treats the roles as a cumulative ladder (a Write collaborator satisfies the >= Triage test), so a Write-only collaborator can close the seeded Open issue 'Improve onboarding'. The fixture is valid: bob-reviewer holds exactly one direct Write grant on the public seeded repository acme-docs (personal repository of alice-dev, so no organization-Owner path applies), holds no team membership and no higher grant, the target issue rd-i1 is Open, and the control shows the same handler closes an issue for a repository Admin.
proposed.subject: closeIssue
proposed.requirement_text: Only users with Triage, Maintain, or Admin may close or reopen an issue from the issue detail view; Write and Read users may only view the status. The system stores the Open or Closed status, operator, and time, records the transition in activity history, and shows it to subsequent viewers; the status transition must not modify the title, description, comments, labels, assignees, or milestone. The closable seed issue starts Open. The detail page offers a “Close issue” button when Open and a “Reopen issue” button when Closed; activating either immediately saves the change without an additional confirmation. Closing displays Closed status and a “Closed issue” activity, and reopening displays Open status. After reopening and reload the “Close issue” button is available again. On the separate protected issue, the Read viewer sees neither close nor reopen button; hiding both controls is required, in addition to rejecting unauthorized requests. This feature builds on the persisted objects, opened pages, or authenticated-session context provided by REQ-5-1-2 (View an Issue and Its Discussion); it must reuse that context and keep pages and data consistent after the context changes.

proposed.explanation: REQ-3-1 requires repository search to display the matching repositories the user is authorized to view, each with owner/name metadata (the metadata exists precisely because several repositories may share a name). The search screen builds its result list from a visibility helper that de-duplicates by repository name alone, so when the seeded personal repository alice-dev/acme-docs and the seeded organization repository Acme Demo/acme-docs both match the query 'acme-docs', the organization repository is silently dropped and cannot be opened from search even though the user has Read permission on it. The fixture is valid: both repositories are Public seed records with the identical name 'acme-docs' (different owners), the signed-in account is alice-dev (owner of one, organization Owner of the other), and the query is the exact repository name from the requirements.
proposed.subject: searchResults
proposed.requirement_text:
The top global search control has searchbox role and accessible name “Search”; entering a repository name and pressing Enter displays repository results directly, without requiring an additional type-filter click. Each repository result has a link whose accessible name is exactly its repository name, while the result also displays its owner/name metadata. Clicking it opens a heading containing the repository name; reloading preserves that overview. A query with no matching repository displays “No results”, including when the visitor returns home and repeats the same query. Seed data provides a named public repository and a private repository inaccessible to visitors; searching the private name exposes no result link for it. Visitors or signed-in users can search repositories they are authorized to view. The system accepts a search query, applies repository-oriented filters or scope constraints, and displays matching repositories with sufficient metadata for the user to open the target repository.

Screenshot reference:
![image](reference/github-repository-search-results.png)
